about.title: Portola Valley Product Liability Claims
about.longDescription: Portola Valley is a small, rural community of roughly 4,594 residents in San Mateo County, but defective products don't discriminate by zip code. A malfunctioning vehicle part on Westridge Drive, a faulty piece of outdoor or farm equipment, or a dangerous household item can cause serious harm just as easily here as anywhere else. Local crash records show 11 injury collisions and 13 injured people in the most recent final reporting year, with activity often clustering around Saturday afternoons — a reminder that everyday errands and weekend routines carry real risk when a product fails. California law generally allows injured people to pursue strict liability claims against manufacturers, distributors, or retailers without having to prove negligence. If a defective product has hurt you or someone you love in Portola Valley, LawProactive can connect you with an independent attorney, free of charge, to help you understand your options.

whyChoose.title: Why Strict Liability Matters for Your Claim

items.title: No Need to Prove Negligence
items.desc: Under California's strict liability rules, you generally don't have to show the manufacturer was careless — only that the product was defective and caused your injury.

items.title: Multiple Parties May Be Responsible
items.desc: Manufacturers, distributors, and retailers can all potentially be held liable, which may broaden the paths available for pursuing a claim.

items.title: Design, Manufacturing, or Warning Defects Count
items.desc: Whether the flaw was in how the product was designed, how it was built, or a missing warning label, California law recognizes all three as valid grounds for a claim.

items.question: What should I do with the defective product after I'm injured?
items.answer: Try to preserve the product exactly as it was at the time of the incident, including any packaging, parts, or instructions. This physical evidence is often central to proving a defect claim. An independent attorney can advise you on safely storing and documenting it.

items.question: Does Portola Valley's small size affect how a product liability case is handled?
items.answer: No — California product liability law applies the same way in Portola Valley as it does in larger cities. What matters is the product, the defect, and the injury, not the size of the town where it happened.

items.question: Do I have to prove the manufacturer was negligent?
items.answer: Generally, no. California's strict liability standard typically requires showing the product was defective and that the defect caused your injury, rather than proving the manufacturer acted carelessly.
